questions.q: Simplify: $\frac{2}{3} + \frac{3}{4} \div \frac{9}{8} - \frac{1}{2}$
questions.solution: Division first: $\frac{3}{4}\div\frac{9}{8}=\frac{3}{4}\times\frac{8}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$. Then $\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{8-3}{6}=\frac{5}{6}$.

questions.q: A reduction of 20% in the price of ghee enables a family to buy 6 kg more for ₹4,800. What is the reduced price per kg?
questions.solution: Money saved $=20\%$ of 4800 $=₹960$ (the price paid for the original quantity falls by $\frac{1}{4}$). At the reduced price, ₹960 buys the extra 6 kg: reduced price $=\frac{960}{6}=₹160$/kg.

questions.q: A sum of ₹4,720 is divided among A, B and C such that A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 5 : 6. What is C's share?
questions.shortcut: LCM of B values (4, 5) = 20 → ratio 15 : 20 : 24; $4720/59 = 80$ per part.

questions.q: The average of 9 consecutive odd numbers is 27. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.solution: For consecutive odd numbers the average is the middle (5th) term, so the numbers are $19, 21, \dots, 35$. Largest $=27+2\times4=35$.

questions.q: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹93. What is the sum?
questions.solution: For 3 years, difference $=P\left(\frac{r}{100}\right)^2\left(3+\frac{r}{100}\right)=P\times0.01\times3.1=0.031P=93 \Rightarrow P=₹3{,}000$.
questions.shortcut: At 10% for 3 years the difference factor is 3.1% of P — divide 93 by 0.031.

questions.q: A trader sells a motorcycle to X at 15% profit. X sells it to Y at 10% loss, and Y sells it for ₹62,100 at 20% profit. What was the trader's original cost price?
A dishonest dealer professes to sell goods at cost price but uses a weight of 750 grams in place of 1 kg. What is his gain per cent?
questions.solution: For every 750 g sold at the price of 1000 g, he gains 250 g. Gain % $=\frac{250}{750}\times100=33\tfrac{1}{3}\%$.

questions.q: Two alloys contain copper and zinc in the ratios 5 : 3 and 3 : 5 respectively. If they are mixed in the ratio 1 : 2, what is the ratio of copper to zinc in the new alloy?
questions.solution: Take 1 part of alloy A and 2 of B. Copper $=\frac{5}{8}+2\times\frac{3}{8}=\frac{11}{8}$; zinc $=\frac{3}{8}+2\times\frac{5}{8}=\frac{13}{8}$. Ratio $=11:13$.
questions.shortcut: Work in eighths directly: copper $5+6=11$, zinc $3+10=13$.

questions.q: If 15 men or 25 women can complete a work in 40 days, in how many days will 12 men and 20 women together complete the same work?
questions.solution: $15\text{M}=25\text{W}\Rightarrow1\text{M}=\frac{5}{3}\text{W}$. So $12\text{M}+20\text{W}=20\text{W}+20\text{W}=40\text{W}$. Total work $=25\times40=1000$ woman-days $\Rightarrow \frac{1000}{40}=25$ days.
questions.shortcut: Convert everything to women: 12 men = 20 women, team = 40 women, job = 1000 woman-days → 25 days.

questions.q: Two trains of equal length cross each other completely in 25 seconds when moving in opposite directions, and in 75 seconds when moving in the same direction. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.solution: Relative speeds: $(a+b)\propto\frac{1}{25}$ and $(a-b)\propto\frac{1}{75}$, so $\frac{a+b}{a-b}=3$. Solving: $a+b=3a-3b \Rightarrow 2a=4b \Rightarrow a:b=2:1$.
questions.shortcut: Opposite: same-direction time ratio 75 : 25 = 3 : 1 gives $\frac{a+b}{a-b}=3$ → speeds 2 : 1.

questions.q: If $x$ and $y$ are positive real numbers with $x^2 + y^2 = 29$ and $xy = 10$, what is the value of $x^3 + y^3$?
questions.shortcut: $x, y = 2, 5$ fits both — sum of cubes $8+125 = 133$.

questions.q: If $a = 2 + \sqrt{3}$, what is the value of $a^2 + \frac{1}{a^2}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{a}=2-\sqrt3$, so $a+\frac1a=4$. Then $a^2+\frac{1}{a^2}=\left(a+\frac1a\right)^2-2=16-2=14$.

questions.q: If $3x + 2y = 20$ and $xy = 15$, what is the value of $27x^3 + 8y^3$?
In $\triangle ABC$, points $D$ and $E$ lie on $AB$ and $AC$ respectively with $DE \parallel BC$. If $AD = 2.4$ cm, $DB = 3.6$ cm and $DE = 4$ cm, what is the length of $BC$?
questions.solution: $AB = 2.4+3.6 = 6$ cm. Triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ are similar with ratio $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{2.4}{6}=\frac{2}{5}$, so $BC = DE\times\frac{5}{2}=10$ cm.
questions.shortcut: Scale factor $\frac{2.4}{6} = \frac{2}{5}$; invert and multiply 4 by $\frac{5}{2}$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $O$ is the circumcentre and $\angle BAC = 55^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BOC$?
questions.solution: The angle subtended by arc $BC$ at the circumcentre is twice the angle at the circumference: $\angle BOC = 2\times55^\circ = 110^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: Circumcentre: central angle = 2 × vertex angle facing the same side.

questions.q: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 13 cm intersect at two points and the distance between their centres is 12 cm. What is the length of their common chord?
questions.solution: The common chord is perpendicular to the line of centres. Its half-length $h$ satisfies $h=\sqrt{13^2-12^2}=5$ from the bigger circle. So the chord $=2\times5=10$ cm (it is a diameter of the smaller circle).
questions.shortcut: $5^2+12^2=13^2$ — the centres and an intersection point form a right triangle; chord = 10.

questions.q: In a regular polygon the ratio of each interior angle to each exterior angle is 4 : 1. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: Interior $+$ exterior $=180^\circ$, so exterior $=\frac{180^\circ}{5}=36^\circ$. Number of sides $=\frac{360^\circ}{36^\circ}=10$.

questions.q: If the radius of a circle is increased by 40%, by what per cent does its area increase?
questions.solution: Area scales as $1.4^2=1.96$, i.e. a $96\%$ increase.

questions.q: A rectangular garden 50 m by 30 m has a 2 m wide path built inside it along the boundary. What is the area of the path?
questions.solution: Inner rectangle $=(50-4)\times(30-4)=46\times26=1196$ sq m. Path $=1500-1196=304$ sq m.
questions.shortcut: Subtract 4 (not 2) from each dimension for an inside path.

questions.q: A solid metallic hemisphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a cone of base radius 3 cm. What is the height of the cone?
questions.solution: Hemisphere volume $=\frac{2}{3}\pi(6^3)=144\pi$. Cone: $\frac{1}{3}\pi(3^2)h=3\pi h=144\pi \Rightarrow h=48$ cm.

questions.q: A cube of edge 12 cm is cut into smaller cubes of edge 3 cm. How many of the small cubes have at least one face on the surface of the original cube?
questions.solution: Small cubes per edge $=\frac{12}{3}=4$, total $=4^3=64$. Inner (unpainted) cubes $=(4-2)^3=8$. Surface cubes $=64-8=56$.

questions.q: What is the value of $\frac{2\tan 30^\circ}{1+\tan^2 30^\circ}$?
questions.solution: The expression equals $\sin 2\theta$ with $\theta=30^\circ$, so it is $\sin 60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

questions.q: If $\cot\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $\theta$ is acute, what is the value of $\frac{3-\sin^2\theta}{3+\sin^2\theta}$?
questions.solution: $\cot\theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow\tan\theta=\sqrt3\Rightarrow\theta=60^\circ$, so $\sin^2\theta=\frac34$. Value $=\frac{3-\frac34}{3+\frac34}=\frac{9}{15}=\frac{3}{5}$.

questions.q: What is the value of $\sin^2 20^\circ + \sin^2 70^\circ + \cot^2 45^\circ$?
questions.solution: $70^\circ=90^\circ-20^\circ$, so $\sin^2 70^\circ=\cos^2 20^\circ$; the first two terms add to 1. $\cot 45^\circ=1$. Total $=1+1=2$.

questions.q: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two points on the ground at distances 16 m and 48 m from its base, on the same side, are $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ respectively. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution: $h=16\tan60^\circ=16\sqrt3$ m; check: $48\tan30^\circ=\frac{48}{\sqrt3}=16\sqrt3$ m. Both agree.
questions.shortcut: Cross-check both points: $16\sqrt3$ satisfies each; if only one had matched, the data would be inconsistent.

questions.q: The variance of 5 observations is 4. If each observation is doubled, the new variance is:
questions.solution: Variance scales by $k^2$ when every observation is multiplied by $k$: $4\times2^2=16$.

questions.q:
The table shows the monthly electricity consumption (in million units) of four states:

| State | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 280 | 320 | 390 |
| Q | 240 | 260 | 325 |
| R | 300 | 280 | 350 |
| S | 180 | 216 | 225 |

The total consumption in 2023 is what per cent more than the total consumption in 2021?
questions.shortcut: Totals of 1000 and 1290 make the rise exactly 29%.

questions.q:
The table shows the monthly electricity consumption (in million units) of four states:

| State | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 280 | 320 | 390 |
| Q | 240 | 260 | 325 |
| R | 300 | 280 | 350 |
| S | 180 | 216 | 225 |

What is the average yearly consumption of state Q over the three years?
questions.solution: Q total $=240+260+325=825$. Average $=\frac{825}{3}=275$ million units.
questions.shortcut: $825/3 = 275$ — the 25 at the end makes the divisibility by 3 easy to spot.

questions.q:
The table shows the monthly electricity consumption (in million units) of four states:

| State | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 280 | 320 | 390 |
| Q | 240 | 260 | 325 |
| R | 300 | 280 | 350 |
| S | 180 | 216 | 225 |

Which state has the second highest percentage increase in consumption from 2021 to 2023?
questions.solution: P: $\frac{110}{280}\approx39.3\%$; Q: $\frac{85}{240}\approx35.4\%$; R: $\frac{50}{300}\approx16.7\%$; S: $\frac{45}{180}=25\%$. Order: P > Q > S > R — second highest is Q.
questions.shortcut: Compare rise/base: P $\frac{110}{280}$, Q $\frac{85}{240}$ — Q's ratio is just under P's, clearly above S's $\frac14$.

questions.q:
The table shows the monthly electricity consumption (in million units) of four states:

| State | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 280 | 320 | 390 |
| Q | 240 | 260 | 325 |
| R | 300 | 280 | 350 |
| S | 180 | 216 | 225 |

What is the average yearly consumption of state S over the three years?
questions.solution: S total $=180+216+225=621$. Average $=\frac{621}{3}=207$ million units.
